title: The Mystery of the Electron Shells
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about electron shells, electronic configuration, and valence electrons.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of electrons the K shell can hold?
questions.explanation: The K shell (n = 1) can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.

questions.prompt: What is the electronic configuration of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has 8 electrons, arranged as 2 in the K shell and 6 in the L shell: 2,6.

questions.prompt: What is the electronic configuration of sodium?

choices: Electrons in the outermost occupied shell
questions.explanation: Valence electrons are the electrons in an atom’s outermost occupied shell.

questions.prompt: Why is neon very stable and unreactive?
choices: It has one electron in its outermost shell
It has no electrons in its outermost shell
It has eight electrons in its outermost shell
It has seven electrons in its outermost shell
questions.explanation: Neon has eight electrons in its outermost shell, which makes it very stable and unreactive.
